questions.q: The value of $\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty}\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-\tan ^{-1} x\right)^{1 / x}$ is
questions.solution:
Let $\mathrm{y}=\lim _{\mathrm{x} \rightarrow \infty}\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-\tan ^{-1} \mathrm{x}\right)$
Taking log on both sides, we get
$$
\begin{array}{l}
\log \mathrm{y}=\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} \frac{1}{x} \log \left(\frac{\pi}{2}-\tan ^{-1} x\right) \text{ form } \\
\left(\operatorname{form} \frac{\infty}{\infty}\right) \\
=\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} \frac{\left(-\frac{1}{1+x^{2}}\right)}{2}-\tan ^{-1} x
\end{array}
$$
(using L'Hospitals' rule)
$$
\begin{array}{l}
=\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} \frac{\frac{2 x}{\left(1+x^{2}\right)^{2}}}{-\left(\frac{1}{1+x^{2}}\right)} \\
=\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} \frac{-2 x}{1+x^{2}}=0 \Rightarrow y=e^{\circ}=1
\end{array}
$$

questions.q: Find the value of the $\operatorname{limit} \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\sqrt{1-\cos x}}{x}$
questions.solution:
$\begin{array}{l}\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\sqrt{1-\cos x}}{x}=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\sqrt{2}\left|\sin \frac{x}{2}\right|}{x}$\\
=$\sqrt{2} \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\left|\sin \frac{x}{2}\right|}{x}
\end{array}$ It can be easily seen that $\mathrm{LHL}$ at $\mathrm{x}=0$ is
$\mathrm{x}=-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ and $\mathrm{RHL}$ at $\mathrm{x}=0$ is $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$.
Hence, $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\sqrt{1-\cos x}}{x}$ does not exist.

questions.q: The value of $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{x^{3} \cot x}{1-\cos x}$ is
questions.solution: $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{x^{3} \cot x}{1-\cos x}=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0}\left(\frac{x^{3} \cot x}{1-\cos x} \times \frac{1+\cos x}{1+\cos x}\right)=\operatorname{x}_{x \rightarrow 0}\left(\frac{3}{\sin x}\right) \times \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \cos x \times \lim _{x \rightarrow 0}(1+\cos x)=2$

questions.q: The values of constants $\mathrm{a}$ and $\mathrm{b}$, so that $\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty}\left(\frac{x^{2}+1}{x+1}-a x-b\right)=0$ are
questions.solution:
$\begin{array}{l}\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty}\left(\frac{x^{2}+1}{x+1}- a x-b\right)=0 \\
\Rightarrow \lim _{x \rightarrow \infty}\left[\frac{x^{2}(1-a)-(a+b) x-b+1}{x+1}\right]=0 \\
\Rightarrow 1-a=0 \text{ and } a+b=0 \Rightarrow a=1, b=-1
\end{array}$
